headline: Use {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, the only configuration inside both gates, and re-test it before relying on it: it clears the pass-rate gate by just {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.gap|abs|pts} points.
lede: It is also one of the cheapest configurations tried, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.low.r1} a month. If a re-test puts it below {criteria.pass_rate.threshold}, no configuration clears both gates and the owner has to choose which gate gives.
flag: The snapshot holds no interval on pass rate, so the pick's clearance rests on a point estimate, and it is the best of {n_candidates|int} configurations tried against the same gate.

caveats.material_if: only if the pick's true pass rate is below the gate, which a margin this thin and no interval cannot rule out; then no configuration passes both gates.
only if the pick's rate was lifted by being the luckiest of the sweep near the gate; a re-run on fresh cases would show it.
only if production carries more multi-hop or ambiguous-entity queries than the eval set, since the pick is below the gate on both and the gate reads the overall rate.

decision.text: Use {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}. It passes {pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1} of queries against a gate of {criteria.pass_rate.threshold}, its p95 latency is {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} against a budget of {criteria.p95.threshold}, and nothing else passes both.

{arm:brisk-s.high.r1} passes more often but its p95 is {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95}. Every Atlas-M configuration misses the latency budget, the fastest at {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.off.r0.p95}. No Nano-XS configuration reaches the pass-rate gate; the best is {measure.pass_rate.nano-xs.high.r1.mean}. Brisk-S without a retry stays below the pass-rate gate at every reasoning level.

The pass-rate clearance of {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.gap|abs|pts} points is the weakest margin on the page, and it sits on the pick. Latency headroom is wider, {criteria.p95.brisk-s.low.r1.gap} under the budget. Multi-hop queries, at {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}, are where the pick is weakest.
Re-test the pick on fresh cases. If it holds, ship it; if it falls below the gate, the owner decides whether the latency budget or the pass-rate gate gives.

claims.text: {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} is the only one of the {n_candidates|int} configurations inside both gates, and it clears the pass-rate gate by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.gap|abs|pts} points.

evidence.caption: Each configuration's overall pass rate against its p95 latency, with both gates drawn; latency on a log scale.

claims.text: A retry lifts pass rate in every model and reasoning setting for almost no added cost, while each step up in reasoning costs far more and pushes latency past the budget.

evidence.caption: Pass rate, cost, p95 latency and gate status for every model, reasoning level and retry setting.

claims.text: Every configuration that clears the pass-rate gate with room to spare costs far more; the cheapest of them, {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}, would run {cost_per_month.brisk-s.high.r1} a month.

evidence.caption: Cost per thousand planner queries for the pick and every configuration that clears the pass-rate gate; all but the pick miss the latency budget.

claims.text: Multi-hop queries are the pick's weakest type, at {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}, and its frozen multi-hop failure collapses the chain of lookups into a single search.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by query type for the pick and the same model with high reasoning; the gate applies to the overall rate, so no line is drawn.
The pick's three frozen failures, one per query type the snapshot kept; not chosen by where failures concentrate.

explore.outcome: Above {pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1} no configuration clears both gates. At or below {pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0} the pick moves to {arm:brisk-s.low.r0}, which drops the retry.

explore.binds: whether the pick has a rival
explore.outcome: The pick holds at every budget from {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} up, because the slower configurations that also pass cost more. Below it nothing passes.

omitted.why: Describes planner behavior (more reasoning plans fewer calls, a retry adds some); no gate reads it and it doesn't change the call.
Listed in the campaign but hold no figures in this snapshot.
The budget is on p95; the median doesn't bind any configuration. It is in the lattice and appendix tables.

omitted.what: Per-task rates for the other configurations
omitted.why: The gate is overall; only the pick's and its nearest higher-reasoning sibling's task rates bear on Watch. Full table in the appendix.
Only one configuration survives, so there is nothing to price; the fallbacks' cost is shown as bars instead.
No gate is per task and no one ran a routed mix; it would be a modeled figure no key states.
Highest pass rates in the sweep, but they miss the latency budget several times over and cost the most; they appear in the lattice and cost bars only.

next.text: Re-run {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} on fresh cases, several times the current set, with intervals reported.
next.settles: Whether its pass rate really clears the gate or the clearance was the luck of picking the best of the sweep.

next.text: The owner declares which gate gives if the re-test fails: the latency budget (then {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} passes, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.high.r1} a month) or the pass-rate gate.
next.settles: The fallback, decided before the re-test result can bias it.

next.text: Add a multi-hop planning directive and re-run the pick on multi-hop and ambiguous-entity queries.
next.settles: Whether the pick's thin margin can widen without paying for more reasoning.

next.text: Declare the production mix of query types, or weight the eval set to it.
next.settles: Whether the overall rate the gate reads matches the traffic the planner will see.

method.text: {scoreboard.brisk-s.low.r1.cases|int} queries per configuration, the same for all {n_candidates|int}; no repeats are recorded and no trials were lost.
Every model at every reasoning level, with and without a retry, fully crossed; no control or production configuration was included, so nothing is read as a change from current behavior.
The snapshot doesn't define what makes a query pass. The failures it records are a missing call, wrong arguments or the wrong tool against an expected plan.
None. Every figure on the page is a point estimate; no correction applies because no contrast is tested.
Pass rate at least {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} overall and p95 latency at most {criteria.p95.threshold}; neither is marked as set after the results.
None: pass is a recorded check, not a judged score.
Cost per planner query as the snapshot reports it, and per month at {meta.volume_per_month|int} queries.
